6. Key Findings & Strategic Recommendations

1. Prioritize Deadstock & VNDS Inventory for Margin Capture
Deadstock delivers the highest average margin ($264.01) and an 100.0% probability of selling above retail. VNDS remains viable at $37.62 average margin. Used inventory should be sourced only at deep discounts to retail, as it clears below MSRP 100.0% of the time.
2. Channel Selection: Balance Margin with Velocity
Evaluate channels on both spread and days in inventory. A channel with a $89.55 average margin but 33.3 days in inventory may underperform a faster channel on capital-turn metrics. Favor platforms in the upper-left of the margin–velocity scatter plot.
3. Model & Colorway Concentration
Pine Green and high-margin silhouettes such as Air Jordan 11 Retro, Air Jordan 4 Retro, Air Jordan 3 Retro offer the strongest pricing power. Avoid over-indexing on low-margin colorways unless sourcing at significant discounts. Scarcity and cultural momentum (e.g., retros, collaborations) drive premium realization.
4. Timing & Seasonality
Monitor monthly margin trends for predictable windows. If specific quarters show margin peaks, align inventory acquisition ahead of those periods and accelerate listings during demand spikes. Conversely, use low-margin months for inventory liquidation rather than new sourcing.
5. Risk Management: Diversify Across Conditions and Channels
Given the wide standard deviation of margins ($159.07), no single model or channel guarantees profitability. Diversification across condition tiers, colorways, and sales platforms reduces idiosyncratic risk and smooths cash-flow volatility.
